gaps.sentence: The evidence ___ by an independent laboratory at present.
gaps.explanation: 'At present' needs present continuous passive: is being + analysed. The lab does the analysing.

gaps.sentence: Over two hundred bird species ___ (record) in the valley this spring.
gaps.explanation: 'This spring' is an open time frame, so present perfect passive: have been + recorded.

gaps.sentence: The temple is thought ___ (build) more than two thousand years ago.
gaps.explanation: Perfect passive infinitive: to have been + built for an event earlier than the main verb.

gaps.sentence: The house is ___ (sell) on Tuesday unless a buyer comes forward first.
gaps.explanation: 'Be + passive infinitive' (is to be sold) expresses an official arrangement.

gaps.sentence: I couldn't use the meeting room because it ___ (clean) all morning.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous passive: was being + cleaned over a period in the past.

gaps.sentence: The manuscript might ___ if you keep touching it with bare hands.
gaps.explanation: Get + past participle (get damaged) is an informal passive common with mishaps.

gaps.sentence: These wetlands ___ (threaten) by pollution every single year.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive with the agent introduced by 'by': are threatened by.

gaps.sentence: The whole engine ___ (strip down) before the fault could be located.
gaps.explanation: Past necessity: had to be + stripped down (phrasal verbs passivise too, particle retained).
